**[Suggestion]** The `||` relaxation is broader than needed for its stated purpose. The comment says the model sometimes describes the change in text without a tool call — but that scenario produces `toolCall=false AND updated=false` (no tool wrote the file), so the test would still fail. What the relaxation actually enables is `toolCall=true && updated=false` (tool called but write failed silently), which the old code caught via the separate `expect(updated)` assertion. The non-interactive sibling test (`cli/file-system.test.ts`) still asserts both properties independently.

Concrete cost: if `write_file` or `edit` is called but fails to update the file (wrong path, wrong content, silent failure), this test passes while the regression goes undetected on the interactive path.

```suggestion
      if (toolCall) {
        expect(
          updated,
          'Expected file content to contain 1.0.1 after tool call',
        ).toBe(true);
      }

      expect(
        toolCall || updated,
        'Expected a write_file/edit tool call or file content containing 1.0.1',
      ).toBe(true);
```

This preserves the flaky-fix intent (accept `toolCall=false, updated=true`) while still catching tool-execution failures when a tool IS called.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

`||` 放宽比注释中描述的目的更宽泛。注释说模型有时用文本描述更改而不调用工具——但该场景会产生 `toolCall=false AND updated=false`（没有工具写入文件），测试仍会失败。放宽实际启用的是 `toolCall=true && updated=false`（工具被调用但写入静默失败），旧代码通过单独的 `expect(updated)` 断言捕获了这种情况。非交互式兄弟测试 (`cli/file-system.test.ts`) 仍然独立断言两个属性。

具体影响：如果 `write_file` 或 `edit` 被调用但未能更新文件（路径错误、内容错误、静默失败），此测试通过而回归在交互式路径上未被检测到。

建议在检测到工具调用时保留文件内容断言：`if (toolCall) { expect(updated).toBe(true); }`，这样既保留了修复 flaky 的意图，又能在工具被调用时捕获执行失败。

</details>

_— qwen3.7-max via Qwen Code /review_

**[Suggestion]** Copy-paste bug: both branches of the ternary call `compactStringForRecording`, so the two `'history'` rows in this `it.each` (`['history', 5000, 200]` and `['history', 5000, 120]`) never exercise `compactStringForHistory` — the `toContain('truncated')` assertion only ever checks the recording marker. The first `it.each` block above dispatches correctly, so this looks accidental. — Failure scenario: a future regression that drops or malforms the history truncation marker (e.g. `buildStringCompactionMarker`'s `'history'` branch no longer emitting `'truncated'`) would pass this suite green while the test name reports the history cases as covered. Today both markers contain `'truncated'` and the production code is correct, so nothing incorrect ships — the cost is a silently void history marker-preservation guard.

```suggestion
        purpose === 'recording'
          ? compactStringForRecording(value, limit)
          : compactStringForHistory(value, limit);
```

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

复制粘贴错误：三元表达式的两个分支都调用了 `compactStringForRecording`，因此本 `it.each` 中的两个 `'history'` 行（`['history', 5000, 200]` 和 `['history', 5000, 120]`）从未真正测试 `compactStringForHistory`——`toContain('truncated')` 断言实际只检查了 recording 的标记。上方的第一个 `it.each` 分发正确，可见此处属于笔误。——失败场景：若未来某次回归导致 history 的截断标记被丢弃或写错（例如 `buildStringCompactionMarker` 的 `'history'` 分支不再输出 `'truncated'`），该测试仍会绿灯通过，而测试名称却显示 history 用例已覆盖。当前两个标记都含 `'truncated'` 且生产代码正确，因此没有错误行为被放出——代价是 history 标记保留的防护测试形同虚设。

</details>

_— qwen3.8-max-preview via Qwen Code /review_

Good catch — fixed in c278145. Both branches of the ternary called `compactStringForRecording`, so the two `history` rows re-ran the recording case under a `history` label. That matters here rather than being cosmetic: the markers are different lengths (65 for history against 79 for recording), so the two purposes get different content budgets, and the history budget was going untested at limits 200 and 120.

discussion_comments.comment_body: **[Critical] Keep vacuous-test findings aligned with the shared severity ladder.** This tells Agent 5 to file a sole-guard vacuous test as Critical, but the same generated brief later appends `SEVERITY`, which says a missing test is Suggestion and permits Critical only when the test asserts the opposite behaviour or was weakened/disabled/deleted in this diff. The project rule appended after that repeats “missing test … Suggestion unless the untested path is itself the defect”, and Agent 7's deterministic efficacy probe also reports an inert test as Suggestion. Thus the same ineffective guard can arrive from Agent 5 as Critical and Agent 7 as Suggestion; Step 4 explicitly keeps the highest severity, so the Critical wins and can block a PR solely for lacking an effective test—the exact severity inflation those shared rules are designed to prevent. Please keep mutation testing as the detection method, but classify the vacuous guard as Suggestion unless it meets one of the existing Critical cases or the review names a concrete incorrect behaviour in the changed code. The mirrored `test-matrix` wording and SKILL table should follow the same rule. A regression assertion should also build the role-5/test-matrix briefs and verify they do not contradict the shared severity text; the current `agent-prompt.test.ts` check only tests that the words `Critical` and `Suggestion` exist, so this semantic reversal remains green.
